title: Iron Alley
tagline: Fly a combat helicopter over a three-road battlefield and win the ground war beneath you.
summary: A helicopter lane-war game in the browser. You fly a gunship in 3D over a valley with three roads, and win by ordering columns of vehicles down them to the enemy headquarters while you clear their way from the air.
description:
Iron Alley is a helicopter lane-war game played in the browser. Two armies, yours in blue and the enemy’s in orange, face each other across a valley with **three roads, called Alleys**, that join their headquarters. You fly a combat helicopter behind a chase camera, but you cannot win alone: the war is won on the ground.

From your depot you order a unit and an Alley, and it drives itself down that road. There are five units: tank, rifle squad, air-defence track, engineers and Breacher. Rifle squads capture outposts, which pay Supply, and engineers mend your vehicles and capture air-defence sites. A unit that reaches the enemy gate breaches it and takes off Integrity, and the costly Breacher takes off the most. A headquarters with no Integrity left is out. The helicopter cannot do that damage itself. Its job is to keep your columns alive and clear what blocks them.

The helicopter has a nose cannon, bombs for tanks and structures, and guided missiles that need a full lock on an aircraft or an air-defence unit. It has fuel, ammunition and armour, resupplies on a pad, and is replaced from a few spare airframes when it is shot down. It can also land beside a rifle squad or engineers, pick them up and set them down off the road. The **computer opponent** is an enemy commander that chooses what to build and which Alley to press, plus an enemy pilot that flies its own helicopter. You pick Easy, Normal or Hard before you start, and a match is meant to run 10 to 25 minutes.

**What is in this build:** one two-side map, Tri-Valley, plus a one-road practice map; keyboard and mouse or a gamepad, with two stick layouts. **What is not:** matches with more than two sides, sound, a campaign or multiplayer. The graphics are plain low-poly placeholders. It is a prototype and is still being tuned.
features: A helicopter flown in 3D behind a chase camera, with momentum, strafing, climbing, turning and a half-turn flip, over hills, tree lines and three roads
Nose cannon, bombs and guided missiles with a lock, plus aim marks on the ground for where cannon fire and a bomb would land
Fuel, ammunition and armour, with a pad at your headquarters to repair, refuel and rearm, and spare airframes when you are shot down
Five ground units to order down any of the three Alleys: tank, rifle squad, air-defence track, engineers and Breacher
Outposts that pay Supply when you hold them, air-defence sites and forward pads, taken by squads and engineers
Airlift: land beside a rifle squad or engineers, carry them and set them down off the road to capture a site
Win by breaching the enemy headquarters until its Integrity runs out; overtime decides matches the columns cannot
A computer opponent with an enemy commander and an enemy pilot, at Easy, Normal or Hard
A top-down map and a clickable order panel on screen
Keyboard and mouse or gamepad, with a Helicopter or Gamer stick layout

controls.input: W / S, A / D or Left / Right
controls.action: Fly forward and back, turn left and right

controls.input: Space or Up, C or Ctrl or Down

controls.action: Guided missile (needs a full lock on a target in front)
Airlift: load or set down a squad while landed

controls.input: 1 to 5, Z / X, G or Enter
controls.action: Orders: pick the unit, pick the Alley, send it. The order panel works with the mouse too
Buy an airframe when you have none left
Left stick climb and turn, right stick forward and strafe, right trigger cannon, A bomb, B missile, right bumper flip, X airlift, Start pause
Left stick forward and strafe, right stick climb and turn. Hold the left trigger for the order wheel: left stick picks the unit and Alley, let go to send
